issue: On federal habeas review of a state conviction, must the court apply AEDPA deference under 28 U.S.C. § 2254(d)(1) to the state court's harmless-error determination before granting relief under Brecht, or may it go straight to Brecht's actual-prejudice test?

sides.position: Courts must apply both AEDPA deference and Brecht when reviewing a state court's harmless-error determination; a petitioner cannot obtain relief without showing the state court's ruling was an unreasonable application of clearly established federal law.
cases: Mansfield v. Sec'y, Dep't of Corr., 679 F.3d 1301 (11th Cir. 2012)

sides.position: A federal court may go straight to Brecht's actual-prejudice test and grant habeas relief without first applying AEDPA deference to the state court's harmless-error determination; if the petitioner shows actual prejudice, the state court's harmlessness ruling was necessarily unreasonable.
cases: Sifuentes v. Brazelton, 825 F.3d 506 (9th Cir. 2016) (cited by the majority as consistent with this reading)

this_court: The Sixth Circuit panel majority holds that AEDPA deference does not apply to a state court's harmless-error determination once the petitioner shows Brecht actual prejudice, so the court may go straight to Brecht.
quote: One set of circuits generally holds that courts must apply both Brecht and AEDPA when reviewing state court harmless-error determinations.
cite: Ervine Davenport v. Duncan MacLaren, 975 F.3d 537 (6th Cir. 2020)
